caseno: Writ Petition No. 3025 of 1996 with Writ Petition Nos. 3026-3029, 3191 and 3192 of 1996.
lawyer:
M Amirul Islam, Advocate ----- For the Petitioner. 
AM Aminuddin, Assistant Attorney- General ----- For the Respondent Nos. 1, 5 and 6. 
Mahmudullslam, Advocate ----- For the added- Respondent Nos. 7-10. 
Abdur Rab Chowdhury, Advocate ----- For added- Respondent Nos. 11-14.
parties:
Matiur Rahman (Md) ------ Petitioner
vs.
Establishment, Government of the People's Republic or Bangladesh & ors ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
4. It is stated in the application that by way of Notification under Memo dated 25th February, 1993 published in the official Gazette vide notification dated 16th February, 1993 by the Ministry of Establishment the petitioner along with others was recruited to the Bangladesh Civil Service Trade Cadre following his outstanding results in the 11 the BCS examination in which this petitioner came first in the order of merit. This notification dated 16th February, 1993 is Annexure-A (l). The petitioner joined his service on 1st April, 1994. After only 9 months of the period of the petitioner's service in the Ministry of Commerce as Assistant Director, Export and Import Control Section, the Government in its drive to reduce public expenditure, amalgamated the aforesaid Section of the Ministry with certain other section rendering it necessary for the petitioner and 8 other officers who were appointed under the said gazette notification to become Surplus Civil Servants. Respondent No.1, represented by the Establishment Division in an official Memo dated 27-5-93 inquired of the Ministry of Commerce, Respondent No.5, that in view of the recent recruitment in their cadre, whether they had any surplus officers and if so whether any assistance was needed for arranging for those officers to be absorbed in BCS (Tax) Cadre which Memo dated 27-5-93 has been annexed as Annexure-B to the writ petition. 

 5. Respondent No. 5, Ministry of Commerce, wrote to respondent No.1 on 15-6-93 indicating that in case the recommendation of the Committee is implemented, then there is strong likelihood of the 9 appointees of the 11th recruitment becoming surplus as a result of the government's drive to reduce public expenditure. The Ministry of Commerce accordingly vide their above Memo recommended the absorptions of 9 officers including the petitioner to the BCS (Tax) Cadre and that letter dated 15-6-93 has been annexed as Annexure-C. On 14-6-93 respondent No. 2 Chairman, National Board of Revenue (NBR), wrote to the Ministry of Commerce informing that there are a number of posts vacant in the cadre of tax & customs and excise. Respondents No. 2 in the letter further invited respondent No.5, Ministry of Commerce, to forward the names of such surplus officers recruited on the basis of the results of the 11th BCS examination who could be absorbed in the cadre of BCS (Tax) or in the Cadre of BCS(Customs & Excise) and respondent No. 2 wanted such communication by 24th June, 1993: The said letter further clarified that the seniority of such absorbed officers would be based on the result of the original competition. A copy of the aforesaid letter dated 14-6-93 is annexed as Annexure-D. Respondent No. 5 Ministry of Commerce duly sent a reply to respondent No. 2's letter on 23-6-93 explaining the circumstances in which the 9 officers of 11th BCS examination recruitment in the trade cadre were about to become surplus. The letter of the Commerce Ministry also stated that in response to an earlier letter by the Establishment Division the said 9 officers' application for absorption into the Tax Cadre had already been sent. The Ministry of Commerce further sent the-list of the said 9 officers to respondent No.1 reiterating their earlier recommendation for taking necessary measure for the absorption of those officers in the Taxation as well as in the Customs & Excise Cadre and the letter dated 23-6-93 has been annexed as Annexure-E. 

 6. Respondent No.6, Internal Resources Department of the Ministry of Finance, in a letter dated 22-9-93 informed respondent No.5 the Ministry of Commerce that it was decided in a meeting chaired by the Principal Secretary of the Hon'ble Prime Minister that if the 9 officers in the 'Trade Cadre were made surplus. then they could be absorbed 'in the Tax or Customs & Excise Cadres Therefore, the letter added that when the Ministry of Establishment announces the surplus status of the said 9 officers then the necessary steps could be taken for their absorption in the Tax or Customs & Excise Cadres. The copy of the aforesaid letter dated 22-9-93 has been annexed as Annexure-F. Respondent No.2 NBR further requested for transferring those officers including the petitioner to the National Board of Revenue on deputation pending the formalities to be observed for making them surplus and completion of the absorption procedure and this letter of respondent No.2 dated 16-1-94 has been annexed as Annexure-G to the Writ petition. The appointment, promotion and deputation section of the Establishment Division accordingly vide a notice dated 19-1-94 named the 8 of those 9 BCS Trade Cadre Officers, the petitioner being one of them, as being announced until further order, to be under Internal Resources Department in order to make arrangement for them to be appointed in the appropriate posts of the respondent No.2's organisation, namely, National Board of Revenue and the said notice dated 19~1-94 has been annexed as Annexure-H to the writ petition. The Internal Resources Division of the Ministry of Finance in a notice published in Bangladesh Gazette announced the names of7 BCS (Trade) Cadre Officers including the petitioner and they were thus appointed on deputation to the appropriate post in the National Board of Revenue and a copy of the said notice dated 1-2-94 has been annexed as Annexure-I Subsequently, on 3-3-94 the respondent No.2 NBR vide a notice duly published in the Bangladesh Gazette announced designations of the 7 officers including the petitioner. In the said notice it was stated that the petitioner had been appointed as Assistant Collector. Customs Excise and VAT Collectorate, Chittagong and the copy of the notice dated 3-3-94 has been annexed as Annexure-J. 

 7. On 11-4-94 the Establishment Division being respondent No. 1 vide Memo dated 11-4-94 addressed to the Ministry of Commerce confirmed that the latter Ministry could take necessary step to announce the relevant officers surplus and make arrangement for them to be absorbed in other cadres and this Memo dated 11-4-94 has been annexed as  Annexure-K. Respondent No. 5 Ministry of Commerce in its reply dated 2-5-94 informed the respondent No.1 that in the relevant section of the Trade Cadre no post had yet been formally abolished and therefore asked whether in these circumstances it would. be appropriate to announce any officers surplus on the expectation that their post would be abolished in the foreseeable future and a copy of this letter dated 2-5-94 has been annexed as Annexure-L, Respondent No.1 in a Memo dated 2-4-95 informed the Ministry of Commerce (respondent No.5) that before declaring the 7 officers surplus it would be necessary to abolish their posts first, Further. it was suggested that steps could be taken for formally abolishing the 7 posts in question and the copy of the said Memo dated 2-4-95 has been annexed as annexure-M. Accordingly, the Ministry of Commerce in a letter to the Establishment Division respondent No.1 dated 3-5-95 formally requested them to abolish 23 trade Cadre posts including the post of the petitioner and 6 others who were already posted in the Customs & Excise Cadre as Assistant Commissioners. A copy of the letter dated 3-5-95 has been annexed as annexure-N to the writ petition. 

 8. The Establishment Division, respondent No.1, duly wrote back to the Ministry of Commerce. respondent No.5, on 8-5-95 expressing their concurrence and agreement with the decision in compliance with relevant Rules in order to abolish 23 Trade Cadre posts which included the 16 posts which would become formally vacant when the   seven persons of 11th BCS Trade Cadre including the petitioner, would be announced surplus. In a similar letter dated 24-5-95 the Ministry of Finance, respondent No.6, also had not objected to the decision to abolish the 23 suggested posts. Copies of the letters dated 8-5-95 and 24-5-95 have been annexed as Annexure-O and 0(1). Accordingly, the Ministry of Commerce, respondent No.5, sent a' Memo on 29-5-95 to the Hon'ble Prime Minister recommending for abolition of the 23 posts while confirming that the legal requirement for abolition of these posts as laid down in BCS (Trade) Cadres Organogram and Cadre Regulation, 1980, have been adhered to, and in the circumstances such posts could be abolished. A copy of the said Memo dated 29-5-95 has been annexed as Annexure-P to the writ petition. On 13-6-95 respondent No 5 the Ministry of Commerce accordingly under a Memo No Bam/ Pro 4/BCS/ Trade 4-22/93/89 formally announced the abolition of the said 23 posts and confirmed that both this Ministry and Establishment Division agreed for abolition and the Ministry had duly granted the abolition of the said posts. On the same date the Ministry of Commerce issued another order, formally announcing the names of the 7 officers, declared as surplus public officers, after the earlier abolition of their respective posts. This list of names included the petitioner as one of the surplus officers of a post that had been abolished. 

 9. Further, the said order issued under the same Memo with issue No. 96 stated that until the 7 officers were totally absorbed they would be entitled to draw their salaries/allowances from their working place under the National Revenue Board, respondent No.2. Copies of both the said Memos dated 13-6-95 have been annexed as Annexure Q and Q (1) to the writ petition. On 21-6-95 the Establishment Division in a letter addressed to the Internal Resources Division announced the selection of the 7 officers, including the petitioner, for absorption in the BCS (Customs and Excise) Cadre and made the necessary directions to the relevant Division for informing the Ministry of Establishment Division on completing the process of absorption and if there was any delay in this regard, to inform the Ministry the reasons for such delay. A copy of the said letter dated 21-6-95 has been annexed as Annexure-R to the writ petition. In the meanwhile the petitioner and six others have been working in their respective posts under the National Board of Revenue since February, 1994, its deputation in the National Board of Revenue having become operative months before the procedures for abolition of posts and declaration of surplus status were finalised. In the first month of his appointment the petitioner received intensive training on the system of imposing value added tax. This was followed by a month long field study regarding implementation and practice as to how to impose value added tax and the study and practical-know-how in the system itself. 

 10. The petitioner's initial period of appointment with Customs, Excise and VAT Collectorate, Chittagong lasted until May, 1994 when he was transferred to Customs, Excise and V AT Collectorate (now Commissioner) Dhaka (North). The petitioner within a very short space of time became an outstanding officer in the field. In July 1994, he was instrumental in exposing a company, the name of Orian Laboratory Ltd who had illegally evaded Taka 40 lakh in value added tax. In the financial year 1994-95 whilst working under Tongi Division the petitioner earned for the country in revenue a sum of Taka 43,83 crore more compared to the previous year and the figure was Taka 23.10 crore more than the target for that year. As an acknowledgment of the petitioner's highly satisfactory performance on 2-1-95 the Collector of Customs, Excise and V AT Collectorate, Dhaka (North) sent him a message of congratulation. A copy of the congratulation letter date 2-1-95 has been annexed as Annexure-S to the writ petition. 

 11. There was shortage of manpower to do the job in the department as the work is ever increasing with overflow of responsibilities. The petitioner therefore, since January, 1996, has been for all intents and purposes, holding charge of 3 posts simultaneously, namely, Assistant Collector (Establishment), Assistant Collector (Commodity and Services) and Assistant Collector (Bond). Due to superb performance and being surplus officer from another Ministry, the petitioner and the other 6 officers soon became a target of resentment by many of the officers of the respondent No.2. The interested group and vested lobby started a machination as to how this input of fresh blood could be excluded from Customs and Excise by denying them in the Customs, Excise and VAT Cadre. 

 12. As part of this machination on 26-10-96 the respondent No, 2 in their weekly meeting made a decision regarding the 7 officers in the following terms, "That as a matter of principle the National Board of Revenue is not in favour of absorbing any officers from other Cadres except in the entry post. The Ministry of Establishment can be approached about the question whether the 7 officers are entitled to be absorbed in the BCS (Customs and Excise) Cadre and if so how should their seniority be determined. After receiving the reply from the Ministry of Establishment a final decision could be made about these officers on making proper evaluation about their performance whilst under deputation;" 

 13. A copy of the minutes of the said meeting dated 26-10-95 has been annexed as Annexure- T to the writ petition. Accordingly, respondent No.3 in a letter dated 3-12-95 informed the respondent No.1 about their decision on absorption and asked for the opinion of the respondent No. 1 regarding the relationship between those 7 officers, petitioner being one of them, and the 13th BCS (Customs and Excise) Cadre vis-a-vis the question of seniority, this indicating that there is no principle so far laid down by the Government as contemplated under Section 6, A' copy of the letter of Respondent No.2 dated 3-12-95 has been annexed as Annexure-U to the writ petition. In reply vide a Memo dated 26-12-95 the respondent No. 1 wrote to both respondent Nos. 2 and 3 stating that in accordance with law these 7 officers had been declared surplus and they have been duly nominated by the Establishment Division for their posts and, as such, they are entitled to be absorbed into the respective nominated posts. The Establishment Division further stated that the question of seniority must be resolved by reference to the relevant rules and regulations in the subject and further referred to an earlier letter by the respondent No.2 addressed to the Ministry of Commerce (Annexure-D) stating that the absorbed officers' seniority would be based on the result of the original competition. A copy of the said reply dated 26-12-95 has been annexed as Annexure- V to the writ petition. 

 14. On 16-1-96 Customs and Excise Association dominated by the power lobby of a vested group interest held an emergency meeting of their Executive Committee. In that meeting the members expressed their concern about the respondent No. 2's failure to return the 7 officers to the Establishment Division in spite Of an earlier promise to do so. Further, in the meeting these 7 officers became the object of evident resentment of the officers who passed the relevant resolution as quoted in the application itself. A copy of the minutes of the meeting of the Association dated 16-1-96 has been annexed as Annexure-W to the writ petition. In order to  create illegal obstruction to the formal absorption of the petitioner along with other six officers the respondent No. 2 held an internal meeting on 5-2-96 and took decision to the effect that at one stage there was shortage of officers in the Customs and Excise Cadre and therefore the• 7 officers were brought on deputation. Then there are sufficient officers in that cadre and therefore the Establishment Division could be written for withdrawing those 7 officers. The Board was of the opinion that if those 7 officers were absorbed in the BCS (Customs and Excise) Cadre, then difficulties might arise about the question of seniority. This would have serious implication in the Administration. A copy of the minutes of the meeting dated 5-2-96 has been annexed as Annexure-X to the writ petition. 

 15. It was further stated in the application that on the one hand respondent No. 2 who has been trying to get rid of these 7 officers on the plea of sufficiency of staff or on the question relating to seniority but on the other hand they are at the same time giving direction to the Internal Resources Division for making arrangement for filling up the vacant posts in the BCS (Customs and Excise) Cadre by recruiting officers through 17th BCS Examination. Clearly there is a sinister motive in this. The respondent No.2 is determined to fill up all possible vacant posts to create a further excuse for denying the petitioner and 6 officers' rights to be absorbed which should have taken place as soon as the Establishment Division recommended the same. A copy of the said Memo dated 5-10-94 has been annexed as Annexure- Y to the writ petition. Respondent No. 3 wrote to respondent No. 1 on 18-2-96 informing its decision made in the meeting dated 5-2-96 and asking them to take necessary measure for implementation. A copy of the said letter dated 18-2-96 has been annexed as Annexure-Z to the writ petition. On 13-5-96 respondent No. 1 wrote back to the respondent Nos. 2 and 3 that there was no scope for withdrawing the 7 officers, and therefore steps should be taken for absorption of those officers. A copy of the letter of respondent No. 1 dated 13-5-96 had been annexed as Annexure Z(I) to the petition. 

 16. In the meantime the petitioner and other 6 officers found themselves in the most unenviable position. They entered the Bangladesh Civil Service with high hopes, expectations and dreams to playa part in their country's progress and development. However, as years went on, their dreams turned into nightmares as powerful lobby in collusion with the vested interests' worked to deny them of their legitimate rights and dues and had in effect caused serious uncertainty as to their future prospect in service by obstructing formalisation of absorption process and their seniority in the unbroken service record which is otherwise due as in the normal course under the law and equity. The petitioner and other 6 officers found that over more than 2 years they have been treated as' on deputation and not being absorbed though that was the main objective for being placed on deputation, the mere formality for completing the absorption process was thus about to be frustrated due to this unlawful and malafide intervention This has caused uncertainty about their future and those innocent 7 officers have been subjected to naked animosity displayed by the interested lobby because the petitioner and other 6 officers have been performing their duties in the National Board of Revenue with a high degree of efficiency and honesty. The honesty and efficiency thus have become the liability for their survival in the Cadre in which they are to be absorbed. One of the interested groups such as those recruited in the thirteenth batch and some of the senior officers and leaders of the Association informally held out a promise that the Association could withdraw its objection if those 7 officers including petitioner would concede their seniority to the 13th batch. 

 17. The petitioner on 2-12-95 wrote to the respondent No. 1 explaining about his high performance at work and seeking assistance in order to bring an end to the discrimination and unfairness of the uncertain position in which he has been kept for such a long time. A copy of the letter of the petitioner dated 2-12-95 has been annexed as Annexure-Z (2) to the petition. The petitioner being fully trained and effective in his post, having spent a long time in learning the expertise and having received in service training, etc. now if the illegal attempt to withdraw him from the National Board of Revenue succeeded then the country would be deprived of his expertise in the revenue matters and the training and experience that he had received, which would be totally wasted and as a result both the country and the petitioner himself as an individual would suffer. Bearing that fact clearly in mind and anxious to bring the uncertainty to an end, being fully aware that, most of the resentment and opposition to the petitioner and other six officers' absorption is due to the question of seniority, the petitioner and the other six officers were forced into a situation for making a grand sacrifice. The petitioner on 25-5-96 and other 6 officers separately on different dates wrote to the respondent No.2 stating that they would be prepared to forego their legal right of seniority and would accept seniority after the 13th BCS Batch. It is to be noted that this was a supreme sacrifice of legal rights made under duress with full awareness of the same by some highly intelligent and talented young officers being under extreme pressure, anxious just to retain the opportunity to simply serve their country in the capacity in which they have been trained, gained experience, proved, to be highly effective and beneficial to the country. A copy of the said letter dated 25-5-96 had been annexed as Annexure-Z (3) to the petition. After receiving that letter on 25-5-96 respondent No. 3 wrote to respondent No. i on 19-6-96 stating that the 7 officers have voluntarily accepted to be counted after the 13th BCS Cadre for the seniority purpose and if the matter is resolved in this manner then it is hoped that nobody would object to their absorption. Respondent No I replied on 8-7-96, reiterating that legally there was no scope for withdrawal of the 7 officers from' their present services. However, since it is stated that the officers had voluntarily foregone their seniority rights and that as a result there will not be any objection from anyone else then the matter can be resolved by wording the absorption order in the appropriate terms. A copy of the letter dated 8-6-96 has been annexed as Annexure-Z (5) to the petition. 

 18. Thereafter on 31-7-96 respondent No.3 wrote to the respondent No. 1 stating that now the 15th BCS (Customs and Excise) Cadre objecting to the absorption of the 7 officers on the grounds of seniority vis-a-vis themselves, and that the National Board of Revenue is also in favour of withdrawing the said 7 officers. The letter further stated that the memorandum that the Board issued on 18-2-96 to the respondent No.3, Annexure-Z, requesting for making arrangement for withdrawal of the 7 officers and stating that, same had always been their stand. A copy of the letter dated 31-7-96 has been annexed as Annexure-Z (6) to the petition. It is submitted that the petitioner became a 'surplus public servant' after the abolition of his post by the Government for the purpose of administrative rearrangement to save public money, in accordance with section 2(e) of the Surplus Public Servants Absorption Ordinance, 1985. Thereafter, there is no dispute regarding the petitioner's status as surplus civil servant within the meaning of the law. It is further submitted that the petitioner once became a surplus public servant, he was duly nominated by the respondent No. 1 being the Establishment Division for the absorption in the post of Assistant Collector (presently Assistant Commissioner) in the BCS (Customs and Excise) Cadre in accordance with section 5 of the Surplus Public Servants Absorption Ordinance, 1985. There are no provisions at all for withdrawal of such nomination. Hence, the stand of respondent No.2 is malafide it being a malice in law as well as in fact to deny the equal opportunity to the petitioner in the service of the Republic. 

 19. On behalf of the Government, respondent No.1, an affidavit-in-opposition has been filed. Another affidavit-in-opposition has been filed on behalf of respondent Nos. 2 to 4. In this case respondent Nos. 7 to 10 are the added-respondents who are already existing officers of the National Board of Revenue. Respondent Nos. 11 to 14 are also the added-respondents. These two groups of added respondents have filed their separate affidavits-in-opposition. On behalf of respondent Nos. 2 to 4 the affidavit-in-opposition has been filed, but no Advocate for respondent No.2, namely, National Board of Revenue has appeared in this case and advanced any argument. On behalf of other respondents their respective learned Advocate have appeared. In the affidavit-in-opposition the learned Advocates for the respondents had taken a common stand as regard maintainability of the writ application. In is their case that since the absorption in a Cadre is a service condition for enforcement of the same, the proper remedy of the petitioner is the Administrative Tribunal constituted under Article 117 of the Constitution and, as such, this writ petition is not maintainable. 

 20. Mr Arnir-ul-Islam, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, submits that the present application is maintainable under Article 102 of the Constitution. His case is that in the instant case the petitioner being in the service of the Republic has not challenged any order passed by any Governmental authority to his detriment, and he is not aggrieved by any order of the Government as such. His case is that, the Government under law has issued a lawful order directing the respondent No.2 National Board of Revenue for absorption of the petitioner in BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre being surplus in other service of the Republic, implementing and carrying out the lawful direction of the Government, namely, respondent No.1. He further submits that in the instant case he is praying for enforcement of Articles 27 and 29 of the Constitution in favour of the petitioner. Since he is praying for enforcement of fundamental right and since he is, in fact, praying for directing the respondent No. 2, National Board of Revenue, to obey and implement the lawful order of the Government, the application before the Administrative Tribunal is not maintainable. Rather the appropriate direction can be given by the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution. It appears that the petitioner has not challenged any order of any Governmental authority by which he is aggrieved. No term and condition of his service is involved in the instant case. The petitioner was directed to be surplus and the Government, respondent No. 1 directed respondent No. 2, National Board of Revenue, to absorb him in the BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre which the Government is empowered under section 5 of the Surplus Public Servants Absorption Ordinance, 1985. He further submits that as per law the present petitioner was nominated by the Government, respondent No. 1 and the Government repeatedly directed the respondent No.2, the National Board of Revenue, to absorb the petitioner following the procedure of law. Me Amir-ul-Islam further submits that the direction which this Court can give under Article 102 of the Constitution, cannot be given by the Administrative Tribunal. 

 21. Since enforcement of fundamental right is involved and since the present petitioner is, in fact, praying for a direction to obey the lawful order of the Government by the National Board of Revenue in the instant case by absorbing the petitioner in BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre, we are of the view that this application is maintainable under Article 102 of the Constitution inasmuch as the Administrative Tribunal is not competent to give a direction as the High Court Division is competent to give under Article 102 of the Constitution. Further, this relates to the policy of the Government which the Government is empowered to do under law. The terms and conditions of service, as such, are not involved. Rather the policy of the Government to absorb the surplus Government Servant in another Department is in question and for that the relevant law is also there. If one Branch of the Department of the Government is not following the lawful order of the hierarchy of the Governmental authority definitely the person who is aggrieved can come before this Court and pray for direction or declaration to implement, fulfill or obey the lawful order of the Government which the Administrative Tribunal is not competent to do. In this view of the matter we hold that the present writ petition is maintainable and the preliminary objection of the learned Advocate for the respondent is overruled. 

 22. In this connection Mr Mahmudul Islam has referred to the case of Mujibur Rahamn vs. Government of Bangladesh, 44 DLR 111 and Civil Appeal Nos. 14-16 of 1995 in the case of Bangladesh vs. Saifuddin Ahmed [50 DLR (AD) 27 = 3 BLC (AD) 6J. We have gone through the judgment of the Appellate Division in both the cases. It appears that the facts and circumstances of this case are quite distinguishable from the facts and circumstances of the aforesaid two cases. Further, their Lordships of the Appellate Division held that for enforcement of fundamental right the High Court Division is competent to do under Article 102 of the Constitution which the Administrative Tribunal is incompetent to do. In this view of the matter we find that the objection of the learned Advocates for the respondents has no leg to stand on. 

 23. Me Amir-ul-Islam has referred to sections 2(e), 4 and 5 of the Surplus Public Servants Absorption Ordinance, 1985. He submits that the petitioner in the instant case is a surplus public servant and he was on deputation under service of the National Board of Revenue, respondent No.2 Since there were vacancies and since the post of the petitioner was abolished and he was declared surplus, the respondent No.1directed the National Board of Revenue to absorb him according to Rules. But from the papers and documents which we have already referred earlier in this judgment and which have been annexed in the writ petition it appears that though the petitioner on deputation has been serving in the National Board of Revenue and though respondent No. 1 repeatedly directed respondent No.2 National Board of Revenue to absorb him, the National Board of Revenue on this plea or other is disobeying and/or showing disrespect to the lawful order of the Government, respondent No. I, who nominated the petitioner under sub-section (2) of section 5 of the aforesaid Ordinance. Mr Islam submits that section 5(2) of the aforesaid Ordinance provides that a surplus servant shall not be absorbed in any post unless he is nominated by the Ministry of Establishment. In the instant case, from the record, it appears that not only the Establishment Division, that is, respondent No. 1 had nominated the petitioner, but it repeatedly directed respondent No.2 National Board of Revenue, to absorb the petitioner after performing all the formalities. But the National Board of Revenue on this plea or that failed to obey and implement the order or the lawful authority. 

 24. The learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for respondent No. 1 cannot dispute the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. No one is appearing for respondent No. 2 the National Board of Revenue. But the learned Advocates for respondent Nos. 10 to 14 are disputing the absorption on the ground that they were already in the aforesaid Cadre and if the petitioner and 6 others are absorbed in their service and given seniority over them, then they will be highly prejudiced and their fundamental rights will be affected. In the facts and circumstances of the case it appears that the absorption is not the main question. The petitioner and six others have not yet been absorbed. If after absorption their seniority is fixed above added-respondents, then the question of being affected or aggrieved of these added-respondents will arise. But that stage has not yet arisen in the instant case. They are only apprehending that if they are absorbed and given seniority over them from date of their appointment, it will make these added-respondents junior to them. The added-respondents' grievance is that their fundamental right will be affected if the petitioner and six others are given seniority above them after absorption. 

 25. In this connection we may refer to Paragraph 38 and Annexure-Z (3) of the writ petition. From the above it appears to us that the petitioner and six others have already written to the National Board of Revenue, respondent No.2 that if they are absorbed, they will not claim their seniority above the existing officers of the same cadre. Rather they will accept the seniority after the 13th BCS batch. Since the said averment has been made supported by this Annexure-Z(3), we are of the view that if the 7 officers including the present petitioner ar absorbed, the added-respondent Nos. 7 to 14 will have no objection as regards seniority and the application of the petitioner and others with regard to seniority filed before the National Board of Revenue may be accepted by the National Board of Revenue and in that case the added-respondents will have no grievance. 

 26. Though as regards seniority the petitioner and six others have already expressed their mind to the National Board of Revenue, even then the respondent No. 2, National Board of Revenue, is not obeying the order of respondent No.1. This is very painful in view of the fact that if the petitioner and others are placed after the 13th BCS batch, then the existing officers who are already in the cadre will have no grievance. It is not disputed that the petitioner is on deputation in the National Board of Revenue with the consent of the National Board of Revenue. It is also not disputed that the posts of the petitioner and others were abolished in the BCS (Trade) Cadre and he was declared surplus along with others. It is also not disputed that there were vacancies in the BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre and for that reason the National Board of Revenue had no objection to take them on deputation. After they were taken on deputation the post was abolished and they were declared surplus and thereafter with the concurrence of the Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Commerce, the Establishment Division had decided to absorb the petitioner and others in the BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre in accordance with the provisions of the Surplus Public Servants Absorption Ordinance, 1985. So, the National Board of Revenue on the matter should have no objection to absorb them in accordance with law. 

 27. Mr Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for respondent Nos. 7 to 10, has raised an objection as regards surplus Public Servant. He has referred to section 2(e) of the aforesaid Ordinance which provides the definition of surplus public servant. He submits that surplus public servant means the public servant whose post is abolished by the Government for the purpose of the administrative re-organisation. In the present case the administrative re-organisation has not yet been made. Since the administrative re-organisation has not yet been made, these alleged surplus employees cannot be absorbed in the BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre under National Board of Revenue, respondent No.2. But Mr Islam has failed to notice that in the self-same section it is also provided that "or any other public servant the responsibility of whose absorption has been taken by the Government." In the instant case the Government had already treated the petitioner and six others as surplus public servant and Government directed the National Board of Revenue to absorb them. So, we do not find any violation of any law as submitted by Me Mahmudul Islam. It further appears that the abolition of the post in the BCS (Trade) Cadre were made and the petitioner and others were declared surplus with the concurrence of the Prima Minister. As soon as the Prime Minister, the head of the Government, has approved the proposal of the one Ministry the other Ministries or Department will be bound to obey it and in the instant case this respondent No.2 National Board of Revenue should have no lawful cause or reason to disobey or defy or dishonour the direction of respondent NO.1. In this view of the matter we find that this very action or attitude of respondent No.2, National Board of Revenue, is uncalled for and contrary to the direction of the Government, respondent No.1 as well as law. So, we are of the view that the National Board of Revenue, respondent No.2, is bound to obey and implement the lawful order of respondent No. 1 In the matter of absorption of the present petitioner and SIX others. 

 28. This petitioner and six others are public servants and they were also appointed through competitive examination and they were appointed as public servants in the service of the Republic. Now this abolition of the post has rendered them, in a very precarious position. Before abolition they were taken on deputation in the National Board of Revenue. Now the post has been abolished and they are declared surplus. But they are still working under the National Board of Revenue with the same scale pay and allowances as they were getting before. They have been nominated, but they have not yet been absorbed. They are on deputation, but they are neither absorbed in the National Board of Revenue nor they were treated as Servants in the service of the Republic in a particular cadre. This has brought this petitioner and others, In a very uncertain position without any fault of their own. In this view of the matter the petitioner is really justified to file this writ application for justice inasmuch as though the Government directed to absorb them in the BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre, they are not being absorbed by the National Board of Revenue, another Department of the Government. So, it appears to us that the present petitioner in fact has got a legal, lawful and genuine grievance for his survival. 

 29. Since the case of the present petitioner and six other petitioners are on identical footing, since the facts and circumstance and the point of law as well as their grievance are same and similar and since all these seven petitioners are on deputation in the BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre under National Board of Revenue and since their reliefs are same and similar, we are of the view that this judgment in Writ Petition No. 3025 of 1996 will cover the cases of other six writ petitioners and these other six petitioners will have the same and similar relief from this Court. 

 31. In the result, all the 7 Rule in write petitions are made absolute in the manner that  respondent Nos. 3 and 4 are here by directed to absorb all the seven writ petitioners in the BCS (Customs & Excise) Cadre according to the direction and nomination of respondent No. 1 in accordance with law, rules and regulations and they are also directed to issue necessary order and/or notification for absorption of the 7 petitioners in the aforesaid cadre service within thirty days from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment. As regards the question of seniority for which respondent Nos. 7 to 14 are very, much concerned, we direct that the National Board of Revenue will be at liberty to consider the question of seniority of the petitioners and added-respondents according to the existing rules, regulations and also on consideration of the application of the petitioners   vide Annexure-Z (3) of the writ petition.
